metadata.concept_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.objective: Explore how health-conscious adults 18-35 navigate sugar-free carbonated beverage choices — from concrete product attributes (zero-sugar sweetener identity, caffeine dose, carbonation intensity, can design, price per 12-pack, availability at their usual grocery) to the functional consequences they produce (no 2pm crash, alertness without jitters, satisfying the soda craving without calories) to the psychosocial consequences they enable (feeling in control, belonging at a rooftop bar without a cocktail, signaling a modern wellness identity without preaching) to the deeper values these consequences serve (autonomy over ingredient choices, vitality, authenticity in lifestyle signaling, belonging with peers who are cutting back on alcohol, pragmatism over purity). Treat category alternatives — Coke Zero, LaCroix, Celsius — as contrast references when respondents describe why a given attribute led them to choose or reject a product.

turns.question: So I'm really curious about the drinks you actually reach for when you want something fizzy and refreshing — I'd love to hear about a time recently when you grabbed a sugar-free soda or sparkling drink, what was going on in that moment, and what made you pick that particular one over something else?
turns.response: Honestly, I grabbed a LaCroix last week when I was just sitting at my desk working and got thirsty. I think I just wanted something with a bit of flavor that wasn't gonna make me feel gross after, you know? Like I could drink it without worrying about the sugar crash or whatever. It was more convenient than getting up to make actual juice or something.

turns.question: Besides the no sugar part, what else about ZeroFizz appeals to you when you're reaching for a drink?
turns.response: Honestly, the taste is probably the main thing. Like, I've tried other diet drinks and they're kind of... off? But this one actually tastes pretty close to regular soda, so I don't feel like I'm compromising just to avoid the sugar.

turns.question: What other things about ZeroFizz let you feel like you're not giving something up?
turns.response: Honestly the taste is probably the biggest thing. Like, it doesn't have that weird aftertaste you get with some diet drinks, so it actually feels like you're having a real soda and not some compromise thing. And I guess the fact that it comes in flavors I actually want to drink helps. Not like I'm stuck with just cola or whatever.
